name: Vivek Ramaswamy
role: Businessman and author; 2024 Republican presidential candidate; 2026 Republican nominee for Ohio governor
summary: Ramaswamy is a conservative, America-first Republican who combines market-oriented economics with cultural conservatism and a restrictionist border policy. He favors deep cuts to the federal bureaucracy, fossil and nuclear energy, school choice and opposes affirmative action, DEI and ESG. On foreign policy he favors reducing involvement in Ukraine and NATO while focusing on China.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 1, 5, 9) attacks bailouts, corporate welfare, lobbied regulatory moats and Section 230 as crony capitalism, and in December 2023 he pledged to end the health insurers' antitrust exemption and vaccine makers' liability shield.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 3) says he does not believe in 'systemic racism' and sees it as an excuse for not fixing poverty and failing schools, though ch. 14 concedes systemic inequality exists through causes like long summer breaks.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: In the September and December 2023 debates he pledged to ban 'genital mutilation or chemical castration' for minors, using federal funding to make states comply.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: In 2021 House testimony he urged Congress not to mandate climate and ESG disclosures, calling them a back-door route to climate policy, while allowing that some mandatory disclosures can be justified.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: In May 2023 he backed a constitutional amendment raising the voting age from 18 to 25, with service or a civics test as the way for younger adults to vote.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: His 2026 Ohio platform pledges to abolish and phase out the state income tax, starting with capital gains; for the federal level his 2023 campaign proposed a 12% flat income tax rather than abolition.

price-stability-first.rationale: In the 2023 debates he called for stabilizing the dollar and a new Federal Reserve chair who puts the priority on dollar stability.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 1, 10) says democracy is messy and beautiful because citizens disagree and thrives on dissent, and in 2023 he said he wants people who disagree with him and 'legitimate disagreement'.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 14) faults Harvard protesters who wanted to escape punishment, saying the willingness to bear punishment for breaking rules is part of what makes civil disobedience heroic.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: In the November 2023 debate he said land-use restrictions constrict the housing supply and make homes more expensive, and called for increasing the supply of housing.

notes:
Positions shift over time (inheritance tax, immigration framing). Research relied on summaries and secondary coverage of his statements; his books were not available as full text.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 27 answers taken from it, 12 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; existing answers not read. Full 490-statement catalog and existing blanks reviewed. Long interviews searched across all themes, with latest Ohio commitments weighed against earlier federal proposals. No inference from party, business career or personal religious practice. The listed revolutionary Marxist propositions remain null. Democracy and consent are supported by explicit defenses of popular self-government; competitive multiparty elections by his express wish for substantive Democratic opponents. Constitutional adherence does not settle every institutional design question. Medicaid fraud reductions do not alone establish cutting legitimate welfare for dependency. Broad technology optimism, animal experimentation, tariffs, immigration levels and general drug legalization remain unknown. Rhetoric is never high confidence. Warrantless hunting searches do not settle the terrorism-surveillance question. Pollution tort enforcement does not exclude all agencies, and data-center conditions are too narrow to settle that choice. AI-assisted fraud detection is not replacement of government decision-making.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-11-07): read the maintainer-supplied full text of Woke, Inc. (2021), his 2021 House and Senate hearing testimony (local hearings corpus), and his own turns in the four 2023 GOP debate transcripts (American Presidency Project), plus targeted web checks. Brought to rules 4: every source tagged words (he holds no office, so there is no record). Answers that rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues were re-sourced to his own words or nulled (collective-defense, voter-id), with the earlier versions kept in reviewHistory; legalize-drugs became 0 (cannabis legalization backed, hard-drug decriminalization disowned) and tax-inheritance 0 (2022 book vs 2023 flat tax). Themes searched: economy (taxes, Fed, regulation, patents, housing), government (separation of powers, voting age, corporate influence), society (family, race, gender), liberty (speech, surveillance, discrimination law), world (Israel, Ukraine, Taiwan, aid). The local corpora hold nothing else of his (no Congress record; Fridman #445 is outside the local set).
